title: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and pulmonary thromboendarterectomy: physiology, DHCA and operative planes
subject: ss-ctvs
refs: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22e Ch 116 (Pulmonary Thromboembolism and CTEPH)
2022 ESC/ERS Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension

steps.say: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension develops in up to four percent of patients following acute pulmonary embolism. Instead of undergoing enzymatic lysis, residual clots convert into organized fibrotic tissue that permanently obstructs the elastic pulmonary arteries. Secondary microvascular remodeling of unobstructed resistance vessels accelerates right heart failure.
steps.tx: Between 1 and 4 percent of pulmonary embolism survivors develop **CTEPH**, driven by incomplete thrombus resolution. The acute thrombi transform into organized, intravascular **fibrotic thrombi** that chronically occlude major elastic pulmonary arteries. Concomitant hypertensive **microvascular arteriopathy** develops downstream in unobstructed capillary beds, worsening pulmonary pressures.

vis.caption: Radiographic evidence of chronic pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular enlargement. Credit: StewardMD.
vis.alt: Chest radiograph showing marked enlargement of central pulmonary arteries and oligemic lung periphery.

steps.say: Hemodynamic criteria formally establish the diagnosis of CTEPH after three months of therapeutic anticoagulation. Right heart catheterization must demonstrate a resting mean pulmonary arterial pressure exceeding 20 millimetres of mercury. The pulmonary capillary wedge pressure must be 15 or lower, with pulmonary vascular resistance greater than 2 Wood units.
steps.tx: The hemodynamic definition requires a resting **mean pulmonary arterial pressure** above 20 mmHg, a normal pulmonary capillary wedge pressure of 15 mmHg or lower, and a **pulmonary vascular resistance** greater than 2 **Wood units** confirmed by right heart catheterization following at least 3 months of therapeutic anticoagulation.

rows: Confirms presence of true resting pulmonary hypertension
Excludes left heart post-capillary passive elevation
Quantifies precapillary impedance to right ventricular ejection
Ensures acute resolvable thromboemboli have cleared

steps.say: Ventilation-perfusion lung scintigraphy is the mandatory first-line screening investigation. Unlike computed tomography, which can miss distal web-like narrowing, a normal ventilation-perfusion scan completely excludes chronic thromboembolic disease. Its negative predictive value approaches one hundred percent.
steps.tx: Radionuclide **ventilation-perfusion scan** is the essential initial **screening modality** for suspected CTEPH. Multiple mismatched segmental and subsegmental perfusion defects with normal ventilation are diagnostic. A completely normal V/Q scan reliably excludes the diagnosis with a **negative predictive value** approaching 100 percent.

left.title: Ventilation-Perfusion (V/Q) Scan
points: Near 100% negative predictive value if normal

right.title: CT Pulmonary Angiography
points: Delineates anatomical extent and surgical accessibility
Demonstrates webs, bands, pouches, and chronic strictures
May miss subtle distal subsegmental disease if used alone

steps.say: Pulmonary thromboendarterectomy is the gold standard, potentially curative surgical treatment. The procedure is performed through a median sternotomy under cardiopulmonary bypass with deep hypothermic circulatory arrest at eighteen to twenty degrees Celsius. Deep hypothermia suppresses cerebral metabolism and allows safe periods of complete circulatory arrest.
steps.tx: Bilateral **pulmonary thromboendarterectomy** is the **curative surgery** of choice for operable CTEPH, performed via median sternotomy under **deep hypothermic circulatory arrest** at 18 to 20 degrees Celsius. Profound systemic hypothermia protects the brain and organs while cardiopulmonary bypass is arrested to establish a bloodless field.

nodes.label: Establish cardiopulmonary bypass and cool to 18-20 degrees Celsius
Arrest circulation for up to 20-minute bloodless endarterectomy interval
Re-establish full perfusion for 10 minutes of systemic re-oxygenation
Repeat arrest for contralateral lung and rewarm on cardiopulmonary bypass

steps.say: A completely bloodless operative field is essential to identify the true endarterectomy plane. Circulatory arrest periods are strictly limited to twenty-minute intervals separated by ten minutes of reperfusion. This intermittent arrest schedule protects neurological function while allowing meticulous bilateral subsegmental dissection.
steps.tx: Deep hypothermic **circulatory arrest intervals** are restricted to strict 20-minute periods alternating with 10 minutes of full bypass reperfusion. Completely stopping flow eliminates bronchial artery collateral back-bleeding, creating the pristine, **bloodless field** required to dissect the microscopic, delicate **endarterectomy plane** into tertiary branches.

rows: Achieve uniform core cooling down to 18-20 C
Replenish cerebral ATP and oxygen debt
Limits risk of postoperative neurological injury

steps.say: The operation is a true endarterectomy, not a simple embolectomy. The surgeon dissects directly into the media layer of the pulmonary artery, establishing a gleaming white cleavage plane. This plane is tracked systematically into each lobar, segmental, and subsegmental branch bilaterally to free the entire cast.
steps.tx: The surgeon establishes a circumferential cleavage plane within the **media plane** of the pulmonary arterial wall. True **true endarterectomy** requires developing this gleaming plane into each individual lobar, segmental, and **subsegmental branches** bilaterally, extirpating the dense cast of chronic fibrotic material rather than performing an incomplete embolectomy.

nodes.label: Incise right or left main pulmonary artery intrapericardially
Identify gleaming pearly-white cleavage plane within the media
Apply gentle eversion traction to follow disease into subsegmental branches
Extract intact, branched fibrotic casts from both lungs

steps.say: Reperfusion pulmonary edema is a unique and dangerous postoperative complication. It typically manifests within seventy-two hours in successfully cleared lung segments, presenting with severe hypoxemia and localized alveolar infiltrates. Management relies on lung-protective ventilation and timely venoarterial or venovenous ECMO support.
steps.tx: A major early complication is **reperfusion pulmonary edema**, arising within 72 hours postoperatively in **revascularized segments**. Sudden high blood flow through chronically unperfused, injured capillary beds triggers high-permeability alveolar flooding with **severe hypoxemia**, frequently requiring prone positioning, nitric oxide, or temporary venovenous ECMO support.

left.title: Reperfusion Pulmonary Edema
points: Occurs specifically in endarterectomized lung segments
Treated with protective ventilation and ECMO rescue

right.title: Persistent Residual Pulmonary Hypertension
points: Reflects extensive inoperable distal microvascular disease
Postoperative pulmonary vascular resistance remains elevated
Treated with oral targeted pulmonary vasodilators (riociguat)

steps.say: Successful thromboendarterectomy yields dramatic hemodynamic and functional recovery. Patients experience an immediate fall in pulmonary vascular resistance and pulmonary artery pressures, reversing long-standing right ventricular dilatation. Long-term follow-up demonstrates a ten-year survival exceeding seventy-five to eighty percent.
steps.tx: Complete surgical clearance delivers an immediate, profound **PVR reduction**, dropping mean pulmonary artery pressures toward normal levels. This hemodynamic unloading stimulates prompt **right ventricular remodeling**, reversing right heart failure and conferring an outstanding **10-year survival** exceeding 75 to 80 percent in specialized high-volume centers.
